text:
Jen Liu: Heads-up — ran the long-context perf sweep (50k tokens) on mixed-precision (FP8/INT8) model and saw TTFT jump ~2.2x during decode. TPS stayed roughly the same.
Marco Pereira: Link to the run?
Jen Liu: dashboard: https://dash.redwood/internal/runs/2026-03-18-llm-longctx. TL;DR: per-kernel timings show the matmul kernel flipping to a slower fallback during decode around layer 28 for some requests.
Jen Liu: Profiler excerpt: 
```
[11:33:41.102] layer_27_matmul int8_fast  1.8ms
[11:33:41.104] layer_28_matmul fp32_fallback 4.9ms  <-- many hits
[11:33:41.109] kv_lookup hit=true 0.2ms
[11:33:41.112] layer_29_matmul int8_fast 2.0ms
```
Tina K: Do we have KV cache eviction events? long ctx + our microbatch scheduler could be thrashing the KV layout and forcing slow dequant paths.
Ryan O: I scanned infra logs — there are index_table evict events around 11:33:41: 
`kvcache.evict index=234 size_before=1.1GB size_after=0.6GB` — lines up with the spike.
Jen Liu: Interesting — I also saw the kernel selector consult per-request seq_len histogram at scheduling time. With microbatching on, the aggregated batch shape sometimes crosses the kernel selection threshold and we flip kernels mid-run.
Marco Pereira: So TTFT suffers because a few requests trigger the heavier kernel even though most benefit from int8 path. Any quick repro?
Jen Liu: Repro steps I used:
1) base config: quant=fp8_int8_mixed, microbatching=enabled, microbatch_threshold=0.02s
2) send 1 long request (50k) + 3 short (512) to cause heterogeneous batch
3) observe kernel_switch_count > 5 and TTFT_p90 spike
Tina K: Can you try forcing a single kernel for decode to validate? env idea: REDWOOD_KERNEL_FORCE=int8_fast_matmul (decode-only). Also try raising microbatch_threshold to prefer grouping similar seq_len.
perf-bot: Perf summary (run 1918765432): TTFT_p90 120ms -> 270ms, TTFT_p50 85ms -> 160ms, TPS ~18 -> 17. Kernel_switch_frequency correlated with TTFT delta.
Ryan O: If kvcache evicts then we also see extra dequant/decompress work. Maybe the eviction threshold is too aggressive for long-context mixed precision. Could increase kvcache_limit or prefer sticky allocation for long requests.
Marco Pereira: Could we add a heuristic: when avg_seq_len > 8k, bias selector towards stable kernels that maintain same memory layout across layers (even if slightly slower per-op) to avoid thrash?
Tina K: Agreed. Also try keeping quant profile consistent between prefill/decode decisions — right now prefill chooses kernels based on batch prefixes and decode consults again per microbatch. We should cache kernel decisions per model+shape.
Jen Liu: Plan: run two experiments and post numbers: (A) force int8 decode kernel; (B) bump microbatch threshold + kvcache_limit 1.3x + cache kernel_choice per model. Will run later today and attach traces.
Marco Pereira: If (B) helps, we can roll a short-term change to scheduler heuristics. Long-term: adjust kernel selector to use a sequence-aware cost model rather than simple thresholds.
Ryan O: Also add telemetry: kernel_switch_count per request, kvcache_eviction_count, and per-layer kernel type timeline. That will help triage automatically.
Jen Liu: Yep — adding those metrics to tracing. Will post results (and flamegraphs) in this thread. :thumbsup:
